newsitem.title: USA: NYSE Mar 31-Apr 4 program trade averaged 20.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE Mar 31-Apr 4 program trade averaged 20.9 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said that during March 31-April 4, program trading amounted to 20.9 percent of NYSE average daily volume of 520.8 million shares, or 109 million shares a day.

The NYSE's program-trading report includes profiles of program trading whenever the Dow Jones Industrial Average moves 50 points or more in a single direction during any one-hour period. During March 31-April 4, there were 11 such periods.
Of the total average daily volume, buy programs accounted for 44.2 million shares daily and sell programs accounted for 64.8 million shares daily.

In all markets, program trading averaged 167.7 million shares a day during March 31-April 4. About 65 percent of program trading took place on the NYSE, 28.1 percent in non-U.S. markets and 6.9 percent in other domestic markets including Nasdaq, the American Stock Exchange and regional markets.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the NYSE, BNP Securities, Natwest, Salomon Bros and Susquehanna Brokerage Services each executed all of most of their program activity for customers, as agent or facilitator. Morgan Stanley executed most of its program activity as principal, for its account.

During March 31-April 4, 25.4 percent of program volume executed by NYSE member firms related to index arbitrage, while 1.2 percent involved derivative product-related strategies. All other types of portfolio-trading strategies combined accounted for 73.4 percent.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more, the exchange said.
